https://theindianawaaz.com/president-mur.text: OTHER TOP STORIES President Murmu lauds Indian community’s contribution to India-Romania partnership Jul 26, 2026 Last Updated on July 26, 2026 1:21 am by INDIAN AWAAZ President Droupadi Murmu has lauded the contribution of the Indian community in Romania, describing it as a vital pillar of the growing partnership between the two countries. Addressing a reception hosted for the Indian community in Bucharest on the concluding day of her State Visit to Romania, the President said that Indians living abroad remain deeply connected to their motherland and make every Indian proud through their achievements and dedication. The President said that her interactions with Romanian President Nicușor Dan and other leaders reflected a strong commitment to taking bilateral ties to new heights. She noted that cooperation between India and Romania has expanded across a wide range of sectors, including trade, defence, renewable energy, digital technology, education, research, healthcare, science and technology, artificial intelligence, innovation, and advanced manufacturing. Referring to the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement concluded earlier this year, President Murmu said its early implementation would open new avenues for trade and investment with Romania and other European Union member states. She also highlighted the productive discussions held during the India-Romania Business Forum, where a high-level Indian business delegation explored opportunities for deeper economic engagement. The President appreciated the valuable contribution of Indian professionals, entrepreneurs, researchers, healthcare workers, and students to Romania’s development. She also thanked the Government and the people of Romania for warmly welcoming the Indian community and ensuring their safety and well-being. https://www.budapesttimes.hu/hungary/mag.text: The Budapest Times Magyar claims 1,000bn forint deficit cut in three months — while blaming Fidesz for the hole The government has reduced the state budget deficit by approximately 1,000 billion forints in three months, the Prime Minister announced on Wednesday in a video posted on his Facebook page. Before Wednesday’s cabinet meeting — at which 38 items are on the agenda — Péter Magyar said that while the Fidesz government had indebted Hungary over 16 years, increasing Hungary’s national debt by 5,000 billion forints in the period just before the election alone, the new government had been handed the treasury with a completely bled-dry budget. “Now the failed prime minister, who is spending his two-month holiday, has come forward claiming that the record national debt is linked to Tisza. The green Fidesz is, of course, also a partner to Fidesz in this. In the National Assembly, it is absolutely staggering how they lie away the facts, while (…) they hand over the budget with a record national debt,” he said. He added that the Tisza government had managed to reduce the deficit by nearly one thousand billion forints by putting an end to unnecessary spending and the free-for-all plundering. He continued: under the Fidesz government, the police force shrank by 5,000 personnel, leaving minimal police presence in most of our settlements, and yet they now hold Tisza to account after just a few weeks for the outstanding pay rise for law enforcement. According to the Prime Minister, the same had been done to social and child protection workers and teachers for years. “Naturally, governing remains our responsibility regardless, and we will continue implementing the programmes we have begun — we will soon adopt the amended 2026 budget, in which what happened is simply that we described reality, whatever lies the Fidesz MPs tell between their two bouts of ranting and clowning in the Hungarian parliament,” Péter Magyar stressed. He added that preparations for the 2027 budget have begun: the budget deficit must be put on a downward path, the national debt must also decrease, the Hungarian budget must be predictable, and both the people, Hungarian companies, and the markets must trust in the budget’s credibility. He also stated that the price of diesel and petrol will be on the agenda at the cabinet meeting — prices that were higher at the pumps for years under the Fidesz government than they are now. “Interestingly, no one is talking about the fact that if a protected price were introduced now, within a week or two there would be a shortage of goods and supplies at Hungarian petrol stations — many Hungarian petrol stations would have no diesel, since prices in neighbouring countries, with one or two exceptions, are even higher than they are currently here,” he said. He noted that Zsolt Hernádi, the CEO of the Mol Group, and other executives of the oil company had been “summoned” to Wednesday’s government meeting. The talks with the executives concerned how to curb “staggering price increases, to the extent that a country can insulate itself from global market trends.” He pointed out that, in an unprecedented manner, Russia has been importing diesel for weeks rather than exporting it, that the situation at the Strait of Hormuz remains unresolved, and that the price of crude oil has exceeded 100 dollars. Regardless of this, the government will provide targeted and effective assistance to drivers of diesel-powered cars who use their vehicles to commute to work or take their children to school — but not in a way that would cause shortages at Hungarian petrol stations, the Prime Minister promised.
